t: Total cost of ownership quote comparison
h:
Supply chain planning · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Total cost of ownership quote comparison

Helena · Purchasing Analyst

The purchasing department of a mid-sized factory closes 60 quotes a month with at least 3 proposals each, and each buyer builds the comparison table in their own way.

When it runs
The buyer attaches the proposals received and the purchase requisition to the conversation with the agent when the quote reaches 3 proposals or the supplier response deadline expires, whichever comes first.
What it delivers in production
One comparison sheet per quote, in a standardized table, with total acquisition cost per proposal, item-by-item technical compliance and a justified recommendation, sent to the approver for the corresponding authority level.
Who decides
Recommends; the approver for the authority level decides
Effort
Calibrate on 25 quotes; 30 days with one buyer

# Purchasing policy: comparison map rules

## Total cost of acquisition (TCA)
- Proposal prices are per unit and before taxes.
- TCA = price × quantity + IPI + stated FOB freight + ICMS (only when the item does not generate a credit).
- IPI = rate × (price × quantity). It always goes into the cost: the company does not use IPI credit.
- ICMS = rate × (price × quantity). It goes into the cost for use and consumption and for fixed assets. For inputs it does not (it generates a credit).
- CIF freight is already in the price. FOB freight with no amount is a pending item: the proposal shows the partial cost "without freight" and **cannot be recommended** until the amount arrives.

## Lead time
- The expected delivery counts from the base date of the quote.
- Business days: count only Monday to Friday, starting the next day, skipping the holidays Nov 2 and Nov 20.
- Late: expected delivery after the need date.

## Payment terms
Normalize in days. "cash" = 0. Installments (30/60/90) = simple average of the installments.

## History
Fewer than 3 deliveries in 12 months: "insufficient history". Score by the on-time rate, not by volume.

## Approval authority
- The approval authority is that of the recommended proposal, by TCA.
- Tier 1: up to R$ 20,000.00 inclusive. Tier 2: above R$ 20,000.00 up to R$ 150,000.00. Tier 3: above R$ 150,000.00.
- It is also tier 3 when the recommended supplier has no purchase in the last 24 months, or when only one proposal meets the technical specification (regardless of lead time or pending items).

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent does not award, does not issue purchase orders and does not send messages to suppliers: counteroffers, requests for clarification and communicating the decision belong to the buyer. A mismatch between the model offered and the specification never becomes a technical equivalent; it is marked as non-compliant and the requesting engineer decides. FOB freight with no amount given goes in as a pending item, not as zero, because treating missing freight as free flips the total cost ranking. One supplier's price and terms do not appear in the justification sent to another.

Common mistakes

  • Comparing a unit price with CIF freight against a FOB unit price without adding the estimated freight to the total cost.
  • Reading a lead time in business days as calendar days and approving a delivery after the need date.
  • Scoring supplier history by delivery volume instead of on-time rate, favoring the large supplier with recurring delays.
  • Accepting an equivalent model suggested by the supplier without going through the technical requester, especially for a spare part.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Buyer's time to build the comparison table for a quote with 3 to 5 proposalsfrom 60 to 90 minutes to 10 to 15 minutes of reviewestimate based on the described routine
Awards to proposals outside the technical specification found in the quarterly auditfrom 1 in 5 to less than 1 in 20estimate based on the described routine
Quotes compared by total acquisition cost instead of unit pricefrom partial and buyer-dependent to 100% of quotes with a comparison sheetprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)

Total acquisition cost (40 units) | R$ 19,296.00 | R$ 19,371.60 | R$ 20,842.00
Lead time and payment | 10 calendar days, 28 days | 12 business days (16 calendar), 14 days | 7 calendar days, 45 days
Compliance and 12-month history | Compliant, approved brand; 93% on time over 14 deliveries, 0 returns | Not compliant: model 22220 CC without EK sleeve; 67% over 3 deliveries, 1 return | Compliant; 100% over 8 deliveries, 0 returns
Recommendation: Supplier A, lowest total cost among the compliant ones and lead time within the need date. B has the lowest unit price, but the model differs and the lead time in business days overshoots the date.
What is missing to decide: validity of A's proposal; origin of B's FOB freight. Approval authority: R$ 19,296.00, band 1, purchasing coordinator.
